note: Recast from the redescription of the soldier of O. makassarensis by Thakur et al. (1992), original in English; only the soldier is described here (the original description of Kemner 1934 covers imago, soldier and worker, but the alate and worker are not redescribed here); in the last row of the measurement table the original prints the pronotal index range as 0.54—0.45 with a mean of 0.59, evidently inverted; it is reproduced as printed and this is noted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule golden yellow to yellowish brown, the frontal gland area distinctly paler; antenna rust brown; labrum translucent brown; mandibles deep reddish brown with a blackish tinge, pale reddish brown at the base; the rest rusty yellow. Head capsule with a few scattered hairs, thorax sparse, abdomen moderate. Body length about 5.15—6.00 mm. Head capsule rectangular-oval, longer than wide, widest in the posterior third; lateral margins nearly parallel and slightly convex, narrowing anteriorly and posteriorly; posterior margin broadly convex. Fontanelle indistinct; eyes and ocelli absent. Antenna short, 17 segments; segment 1 longest and largest; segment 2 cylindrical, about 2 times segment 3; segment 4 longer and wider than 3; segment 5 slightly wider, about as long as 3; the remaining segments globose, lengthening posteriorly; terminal segment oval (in 1 specimen the left antenna has 16 segments, segment 5 being subdivided). Anteclypeus a narrow transparent glabrous band; postclypeus not clearly delimited from the frons. Labrum nearly triangular, lanceolate, lateral margins slightly convex, narrowing forwards to a narrow rounded apex, with two rows of long hairs. Mandibles sword-shaped, slightly incurved apically, more than half the head length (head-mandible index 0.53); left mandible with 1 small but distinct lateral tooth near the upper edge at the middle, the inner edge convex below the tooth; right mandible with a very small serrate projection in the corresponding position. Postmentum nearly rectangular, lateral margins nearly parallel, widest in the basal third, anterior margin straight, posterior margin slightly concave with a distinct median swelling. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior lobe upturned, wider than long (pronotal index 0.54—0.57), anterior margin convex with a distinct median notch, posterior margin also with a distinct median notch; mesonotum narrower than the pronotum, with a median notch on the posterior margin; metanotum almost as wide as the pronotum, posterior margin slightly convex. Legs slender and hairy, tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate and hairy; cerci 2-segmented, about 0.10—0.13 mm long; styli 1-segmented, about 0.10 mm long. Measurements (mm, 5 soldiers, range/mean): body length about 5.15—6.00/5.60; head length (with mandibles) 2.75—3.10/2.98; head length to the mandible base 1.90—2.05/1.98; maximum head width 1.60—1.75/1.68; head width at the mandible base 1.00—1.13/1.07; head width at the antennal base 1.45—1.55/1.52; head height 1.00—1.05/1.03; head index I 0.83—0.88/0.85; left mandible length 1.00—1.05/1.03, right mandible length 1.00—1.05/1.03; head-mandible index I 0.51—0.54/0.52; distance from the tooth to the mandible apex 0.60—0.65/0.62; mandibular tooth index 0.57—0.63/0.60; minimum (median) postmentum length 1.25—1.35/1.28; maximum postmentum width 0.67—0.75/0.70; minimum postmentum width 0.45—0.48/0.47; pronotum length 0.65—0.75/0.69; maximum pronotum width 1.08—1.23/1.16; pronotal index 0.54—0.45/0.59.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the key it is contrasted with O. grandiceps: this species is smaller (head length with mandibles 2.75—3.10 mm, grandiceps 3.70—3.80 mm; head length to the mandible base 1.90—2.05 mm, grandiceps 2.45—2.60 mm; head width 1.60—1.75 mm, grandiceps 2.10—2.25 mm), antennal segment 2 is nearly 2 times segment 3, and the mandibles are longer than half the head length to the lateral mandible bases (head-mandible index 0.5—0.54).
